events.objective: Establish the symptom timeline and blast radius around the report time (~10:05 UTC, current 11:59 UTC). Using query_logs and query_metrics: (1) precise onset time of api-gateway p99 latency rise and 504s on /v1/portfolio/*; (2) which other services/endpoints show latency or error degradation in the same window (is it portfolio-specific or gateway-wide?); (3) error signatures in gateway logs (upstream connection resets, HTTP/2 errors, timeouts, 5xx from downstream); (4) resource trends (CPU, memory, connection/pool saturation) on api-gateway and its upstreams. Report whether the gateway itself looks resource-saturated or merely waiting on downstream.

Enumerate everything that changed across ALL services in the hours before onset (~08:00–10:30 UTC), not only api-gateway. Using get_deployments and get_config_changes: list deploys and config/flag changes with timestamps, affected services, and whether the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade is one of several changes. Also use get_service_dependencies to map the call path behind /v1/portfolio/* (what api-gateway calls and what those call), and search_historical_incidents for prior similar portfolio-latency or gateway-upgrade incidents and how they were resolved. Highlight any change to a downstream component the portfolio path depends on.

Correlate changes against the confirmed onset time from task a: determine which of the changes enumerated in task b is closest to and preceding the latency onset, whether it touches a service on the portfolio call path, and whether the gateway upgrade timing matches the onset or is merely coincident. Conclude which change is the prime suspect and which are ruled out, including whether a downstream change better explains gateway p99 and 504s.

args.query: portfolio page latency timeout gateway upgrade HTTP/2

events.statement: api-gateway p99 latency stepped up between the 09:40 and 09:50 buckets: 206.74ms avg (max 223.22) at 09:40 -> 3119.97ms avg (max 4624.18) at 09:50, and stayed ~4300ms through 11:50. Baseline 08:00-09:40 was flat ~205-215ms.
api-gateway error_rate rose in the same 09:50 bucket from ~0.2% baseline to 4.44% (max 7.74%), plateauing ~7.1-7.4% through 11:50.

Gateway warning logs are dominated by one signature: 252 of 254 WARN entries are 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504', first seen 2026-03-10T09:53:53Z. No HTTP/2 or TLS error signature appears in the sampled WARNs.

portfolio-service shows the same latency step (180.55ms avg at 09:40 -> 3031.47ms at 09:50 -> ~4150ms thereafter) and its ERROR logs are connection-pool exhaustion: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (270x) and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)', first seen 09:53:19/09:54:29.

api-gateway itself is not resource-saturated: CPU stayed flat at ~42% (41.81 at 09:50, max only 46.78 over the whole window) and memory flat at ~58%, with no restarts evident — the resource step is absent even as latency rose 20x.
portfolio-service CPU is also flat (~35-36%, 35.64 at 09:50), so its pool exhaustion is not CPU-driven — it is blocked waiting on its database/connection pool.

events.description: No metric or log query was run against the database behind portfolio-service (no db component metrics/logs collected) to show whether the DB is slow/unreachable versus pool misconfiguration.

Blast radius across other services/endpoints is only established via the absence of non-portfolio endpoint names in gateway logs; no per-endpoint or per-service latency queries were run for other consumers of api-gateway.
Both gateway (254 matched) and portfolio-service (505 matched) log results were truncated:true (40 and 30 entries returned), so the log inventory is incomplete.
Exact sub-bucket onset between 09:40 and 09:50 could not be pinned: metrics are 600s (10-min) buckets and only 24 points were returned, so onset is bounded to 09:40-09:50, not to the minute.

events.answer: Onset was between 09:40 and 09:50 UTC (much earlier than the 10:05 report): api-gateway p99 jumped from ~206ms to ~3120ms and 504s on /v1/portfolio/holdings began at 09:53:53. The degradation is portfolio-specific — the only failing endpoint is GET /v1/portfolio/holdings, and portfolio-service shows the identical latency step plus JDBC/Hikari connection-pool exhaustion, while the gateway itself is not resource-saturated (CPU flat ~42%, memory flat ~58%). The gateway appears to be waiting on portfolio-service, which in turn is blocked on its DB connection pool.

events.statement: Only two changes exist across all services between 00:00 and 12:00 UTC on 2026-03-10: deployment dep-5220 (api-gateway) and config change cfg-2207 (portfolio-service). The 07:30–10:30 window initially returned just these plus a benign order-service log-sampling tweak (cfg-2199, 07:00 UTC, log.sampling_rate 0.1→0.2).

Deployment dep-5220 on api-gateway v9.3.0 was deployed at 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z by platform-team: 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' with changes envoy 1.29 -> 1.30 and 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service'. Status is 'live' and rolled_back_at is null — it had NOT been rolled back as of the latest data.

Config change cfg-2207 reduced portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, authored by infra-automation ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource') — a 10x reduction of the DB connection pool on the service that serves /v1/portfolio/*, occurring ~1h52m after the gateway deploy.

The /v1/portfolio/* path is: api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http); portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache); market-data-service -> redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http). ledger-db and redis-cache are flagged shared=true, used by several services (ledger-db also by order-service, payment-service, auth-service... per the gateway graph).

Precedent HIST-116 (2025-12-18, api-gateway only, match_score 4) is an HTTP/2 regression after an envoy gateway upgrade: symptoms '504 at gateway, upstream resets, timeouts', root cause 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default', category bad_deployment, resolved by rolling back the gateway. HIST-102 (2025-09-02, portfolio-service + ledger-db, match_score 3) has the same user-visible symptoms ('portfolio page timeouts', '504 at gateway') but a different cause: 'Unplanned ledger-db primary failover; 6 min of refused connections', resolved by failover + adding retry.

The gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (dep-5220) is therefore one of exactly two changes in the incident window, and it is the only one affecting two services' upstream protocol; the other (cfg-2207) targets a downstream dependency of the portfolio path. Note the ordering tension: the reported onset is ~10:05 UTC, 2h05m after dep-5220 but 13 minutes after cfg-2207; metrics were not checked in this task, so I cannot yet say which timestamp the latency onset actually tracks.

events.answer: Across ALL services in 00:00–12:00 UTC on 2026-03-10 there were exactly two relevant changes: deploy dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, 08:00 UTC, envoy 1.29→1.30 + HTTP/2 to portfolio-service/order-service, still live, NOT rolled back) and config change cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50→5, 09:52 UTC). The gateway HTTP/2 upgrade is real and is one of exactly two changes, but cfg-2207 lands ~52 min later and directly throttles a connection pool the portfolio path depends on; the portfolio call path is api-gateway → portfolio-service → {ledger-db (shared), market-data-service → {redis-cache (shared), exchange-gateway}, redis-cache (shared)}. Precedents exist for both an envoy HTTP/2 upgrade causing 504s (HIST-116, fixed by gateway rollback) and portfolio 504s with a DB root cause (HIST-102, ledger-db failover).

events.statement: Exact change timeline across all services 07:00-11:59 UTC is only two candidates: dep-5220 (api-gateway v9.3.0, 2026-03-10T08:00:00Z, 'envoy 1.29 -> 1.30', 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service', status 'live', rolled_back_at null) and cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, infra-automation, 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'). A portfolio-service-scoped deploy query returns count 0. So gateway deploy is 1h50m BEFORE the 09:50 latency onset bucket; the pool config change is 2m before onset and 13m before the 10:05 report.

cfg-2207 (09:52:00Z) is the only change touching a service on the portfolio call path immediately preceding onset, and it throttled the exact resource that then exhausted: T1's pool error shows total=5, idle=0, waiting=43 — the 'total=5' matches cfg-2207's new db.pool.max_size=5 (old 50), so the pool ceiling is literally the new config value. The pool exhaustion errors begin 09:53:19/09:54:29, ~79s after the change (consistent with the 3000ms acquire timeout).

The change is on the correct path: the /v1/portfolio/* call path from the authoritative dependency graph is api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http), and portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache). Downstream changes to ledger-db/redis-cache are NOT needed to explain the failure — the broken component (portfolio-service JDBC pool) is directly on the path and the config change targets it in-place.

The gateway HTTP/2 upgrade is merely coincident, not causal: it shipped 08:00 UTC, ~1h50m before onset, while identical symptoms (504s on /v1/portfolio/*, upstream timeouts) are fully explained by the downstream pool exhaustion. T1 additionally found NO HTTP/2/TLS error signature in gateway logs (254 WARNs, 252 are 'upstream timeout portfolio-service') and the gateway is not resource-saturated (CPU flat ~42%, memory ~58%), so the HTTP/2 regression fingerprint from HIST-116 (upstream resets/HTTP/2 errors) is absent.

Precedent search supports a DB/pool-cause lead over the HTTP/2 lead for portfolio 504s: HIST-102 (2025-09-02, portfolio-service + ledger-db, match_score 3.5) has identical user-visible symptoms ('portfolio page timeouts', '504 at gateway') with root cause 'Unplanned ledger-db primary failover; 6 min of refused connections'. This is a lead only — the current cause is an induced pool-size misconfiguration, not an unplanned failover, but it confirms the 504-at-gateway symptom family maps to the portfolio-service -> ledger-db DB leg.

No rollout of a fix is visible as of latest data: dep-5220 remains status 'live' with rolled_back_at null, and no deployment or config change appears after 09:52 UTC through 11:59 UTC — so neither suspected change has been reverted while the incident is ongoing.

events.answer: Prime suspect: config change cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52 UTC) — it is on the portfolio call path, lands ~2 min before the 09:50 onset bucket, and its new value (5) is exactly the pool ceiling seen exhausted (total=5, idle=0, waiting=43) at 09:53:19. The api-gateway HTTP/2 upgrade dep-5220 (08:00 UTC, ~1h50m earlier) is merely coincident and is ruled out as prime suspect: its HTTP/2 fingerprint is absent and the gateway is not resource-saturated. No change to a shared downstream (ledger-db/redis-cache) is needed; the downstream change here is the pool config on portfolio-service itself, which better explains gateway p99 and 504s than the gateway upgrade.

events.title: cfg-2207 shrank portfolio-service JDBC pool 50→5, causing pool exhaustion → downstream timeouts → gateway 504s
Reporter's suspicion: dep-5220 gateway HTTP/2-to-upstream upgrade broke upstream connections (HIST-116-style regression)

events.summary: H1 is well grounded: cfg-2207 (09:52Z, pool 50->5), the exact numeric match between the new ceiling and the exhausted pool (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43), the flat CPU on both gateway and portfolio-service, 252/254 gateway WARNs being 'upstream timeout portfolio-service -> 504', and the identical latency step on both tiers are all VERIFIED findings. H2 (reporter's HTTP/2 suspicion) is adequately dismissed: dep-5220 landed 08:00Z, ~110 min before the 09:50-09:53 onset, no HTTP/2/TLS signature appears, and the gateway is not resource-saturated. H4 is a subordinated variant of H1 with one unbacked hop. The main un-tested rival is H3 (shared ledger-db/redis-cache degradation), which was never independently excluded because no shared-datastore or pool metrics were queried. Also, onset rests on 10-min buckets so the sub-bucket order of the latency step vs. the 09:52 change is unresolved. Both are obtainable and could change ranking or story; hence needs_evidence rather than accept. Not inconclusive — the decisive fingerprint (total=5 == new config value) is already documented.

Inference: the shared datastores are NORMAL, not degraded, around 09:50-09:53Z. Therefore portfolio-service's connection-pool exhaustion ('total=5, idle=0, waiting=43', F4/F14) is self-inflicted by cfg-2207's pool ceiling of 5, not the downstream effect of a stalled shared datastore — H3 is not supported and the HIST-102 'ledger-db failover' mechanism does not reproduce here (no refused connections, no connection spike).

events.summary: H1 is now adequately proven. The round-1 blocker (untested H3) was closed: ledger-db is verifiably flat/declining across onset (F19: cpu ~30%, replication_lag ~40ms, slow_queries ~1/min; F20: connections_active drifting DOWN 62->55, opposite of a stall; F21: zero WARN+ logs), and redis-cache shows only one unrelated post-onset internal-metrics WARN (F22). The decisive fingerprint is the numeric identity between cfg-2207's new db.pool.max_size=5 and the exhausted pool ('total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43'), combined with pre-existing demand ~11.9 > 5 (deterministic saturation requiring no load rise — request_rate flat, F29), flat CPU on both tiers (F5, F6), and 252/254 gateway WARNs being 'upstream timeout portfolio-service -> 504' (F3). H2 (reporter's HTTP/2 suspicion) is contradicted on timing (08:00 vs 09:53 onset), absent HTTP/2/TLS signature, and non-saturated gateway. H3 contradicted by datastore evidence. H4 is H1 plus an unbacked and contradicted second hop (F19-F22, F29). Residual gaps (redis-cache metric series unretrieved; truncated log samples) are minor and cannot promote a rival above H1. No further tool spend is justified during a live outage.

The api-gateway HTTP/2 upgrade dep-5220 (08:00 UTC, ~1h50m earlier) is merely coincident and is ruled out as prime suspect: its HTTP/2 fingerprint is absent and the gateway is not resource-saturated. No change to a shared downstream (ledger-db/redis-cache) is needed; the downstream change here is the pool config on portfolio-service itself, which better explains gateway p99 and 504s than the gateway upgrade.

tasks.objective: Test H3 independently: query ledger-db and redis-cache metrics (query latency, active connections, CPU, error/refusal rate, failover events) and logs for 09:45-10:10Z, compared against a pre-09:45 baseline (e.g., 08:30-09:45Z). Determine whether both shared datastores are normal/flat or degraded around 09:50-09:53Z. Report a clear verdict on whether any shared-datastore degradation coincides with the portfolio latency onset.
tasks.answer: H3 is NOT supported. ledger-db shows no degradation coinciding with the 09:50 latency onset: connections_active, slow_queries_per_min, replication_lag_ms and cpu_pct are all flat across the 08:30–09:45 baseline and the 09:45–10:10 onset window (CPU ~30%, lag ~40ms, slow queries ~1/min, active connections actually drift DOWN from ~62 to ~55). ledger-db produced zero WARN+ logs in 09:45–10:10Z; redis-cache produced exactly one unrelated WARN (slow /internal/metrics request at 09:58:57). Neither shared datastore is degraded around 09:50–09:53Z, so the pool exhaustion in portfolio-service (F4/F14) is self-inflicted by cfg-2207's pool-size cut, not caused by a stalled shared datastore. Caveat: I ran out of budget before retrieving redis-cache's hit_ratio/cpu/evictions/connected_clients series, so the redis verdict rests on logs alone.

tasks.objective: Confirm H1 from independent metrics and pin sub-bucket onset order: query portfolio-service JDBC/Hikari pool metrics (active/in_use, idle, waiting, acquire latency) at the finest available granularity for 09:40-10:00Z, and api-gateway p99 plus portfolio-service request latency at the finest available granularity within the 09:40-09:50 bucket. Answer: did active connections cross the new ceiling of 5 exactly at/after 09:52Z, and did the latency step begin after 09:52Z rather than earlier in the bucket? Report whether the config change verifiably precedes the latency step.
tasks.answer: Yes on both counts, at 1-minute resolution: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was ~11.9 at 09:52 and then pinned at exactly 5.0 from the 09:53 bucket onward (the active count hit the new ceiling of 5 immediately after 09:52Z), and the latency step began at 09:53 — portfolio-service p99 172.69ms@09:52 -> 4250.91ms@09:53 and api-gateway p99 200.33ms@09:52 -> 4418.76ms@09:53 — with no elevation anywhere in 09:40-09:52. The cfg-2207 pool change (09:52:00Z) verifiably precedes the latency step (first elevated bucket 09:53), so H1's causal ordering holds; the only caveat is 1-minute bucket resolution cannot separate sub-minute ordering.

critiques.summary: H1 is well grounded: cfg-2207 (09:52Z, pool 50->5), the exact numeric match between the new ceiling and the exhausted pool (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43), the flat CPU on both gateway and portfolio-service, 252/254 gateway WARNs being 'upstream timeout portfolio-service -> 504', and the identical latency step on both tiers are all VERIFIED findings. H2 (reporter's HTTP/2 suspicion) is adequately dismissed: dep-5220 landed 08:00Z, ~110 min before the 09:50-09:53 onset, no HTTP/2/TLS signature appears, and the gateway is not resource-saturated. H4 is a subordinated variant of H1 with one unbacked hop. The main un-tested rival is H3 (shared ledger-db/redis-cache degradation), which was never independently excluded because no shared-datastore or pool metrics were queried. Also, onset rests on 10-min buckets so the sub-bucket order of the latency step vs. the 09:52 change is unresolved. Both are obtainable and could change ranking or story; hence needs_evidence rather than accept. Not inconclusive — the decisive fingerprint (total=5 == new config value) is already documented.

challenges.issue: Temporal precision: the latency step is only bounded to the 09:40-09:50 vs 09:50-10:00 10-min buckets. cfg-2207 is at 09:52Z, inside the 09:50 bucket. It is not pinned that the portfolio-service/gateway latency rise began AFTER 09:52 rather than earlier in the bucket. The pool error logs (09:53:19) and gateway 504s (09:53:53) do follow the change, so this is likely a bucket-averaging artifact, but the causal ordering of the metric step vs. the config change is not tightly established.

The shared-datastore rival (ledger-db/redis-cache slow or failing, which would stall portfolio-service queries and fill any pool size) was never tested: no db/cache latency, connection, failover, or error metrics were queried for 09:50-10:05Z. H3 is dismissed largely by the internal fit of H1, not by contradicting evidence on the datastores themselves.

Ruling out dep-5220 rests partly on absence of an HTTP/2/connection-reset signature in a TRUNCATED log sample (40 of 254 gateway WARNs returned, 30 of 505 portfolio-service entries). Absence in a truncated sample is weak, though the 110-min timing gap independently excludes dep-5220 as the trigger regardless of signature.

The 'active count pins at the new ceiling of 5' claim rests on the Hikari log line rather than an independently queried pool metric (db_pool_in_use / active-idle-waiting), which was listed as an available metric but never queried.

evidence_requests.question: Query ledger-db and redis-cache metrics (query latency, active connections, CPU, error/refusal rate, failover events) and logs for 09:45-10:10Z. Are they normal/flat, or degraded around 09:50-09:53Z? Compare to a pre-09:45 baseline.
evidence_requests.rationale: H3 posits a shared-datastore degradation as the origin; this was never tested. If ledger-db/redis-cache are normal, H3 is truly refuted and H1 stands alone. If degraded, the fault story changes (compound/H4-like) and could reorder the ranking.

evidence_requests.question: Query portfolio-service JDBC pool metrics (db_pool_in_use / active, idle, waiting, acquire latency) at fine granularity for 09:40-10:00Z, and gateway p99 plus portfolio-service request latency at the finest available granularity in the 09:40-09:50 bucket. critiques.summary: H1 is now adequately proven. The round-1 blocker (untested H3) was closed: ledger-db is verifiably flat/declining across onset (F19: cpu ~30%, replication_lag ~40ms, slow_queries ~1/min; F20: connections_active drifting DOWN 62->55, opposite of a stall; F21: zero WARN+ logs), and redis-cache shows only one unrelated post-onset internal-metrics WARN (F22). The sub-bucket onset question was answered at the achievable 1-minute resolution: db_pool_in_use pinned at exactly 5.0 from the 09:53 bucket (F25), and p99 stepped in the same bucket in both portfolio-service and api-gateway with no elevation 09:40-09:52 (F26, F27, F30), so the 09:52 cfg-2207 change verifiably precedes (or is simultaneous at resolution limit with) the latency step. The decisive fingerprint is the numeric identity between cfg-2207's new db.pool.max_size=5 and the exhausted pool ('total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43'), combined with pre-existing demand ~11.9 > 5 (deterministic saturation requiring no load rise — request_rate flat, F29), flat CPU on both tiers (F5, F6), and 252/254 gateway WARNs being 'upstream timeout portfolio-service -> 504' (F3). H2 (reporter's HTTP/2 suspicion) is contradicted on timing (08:00 vs 09:53 onset), absent HTTP/2/TLS signature, and non-saturated gateway. H3 contradicted by datastore evidence. H4 is H1 plus an unbacked and contradicted second hop (F19-F22, F29). Residual gaps (redis-cache metric series unretrieved; truncated log samples) are minor and cannot promote a rival above H1. No further tool spend is justified during a live outage.

challenges.issue: Redis-cache metric series (hit_ratio_pct, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, connected_clients) for 08:30-10:10Z were never retrieved, so the 'redis is normal' half of the H3 verdict rests on logs alone. This is non-blocking because the broken component sits in-place on the portfolio-service JDBC pool, not behind redis, and the exact value/timing fingerprint already identifies cfg-2207.

Gateway and portfolio-service log results were truncated (254 and 505 matched, ~30-40 returned each), so the log inventory is incomplete and a rare HTTP/2 or reset signature cannot be formally excluded from the full set; but the 252/254 timeout dominance plus the absent resource saturation make this immaterial to ranking.

Sub-minute ordering within the 09:52 bucket is unresolvable (config at 09:52:00, first affected bucket 09:53); ordering is verified only to 1-minute resolution. Acceptable because pre-existing demand (~11.9) exceeded the new ceiling (5) regardless of sub-minute timing.
